findings.quote: Dropping the negative sign that comes from differentiating 1/(2ax+b), giving 2av² instead of the correct −2av³.
findings.note: Dropping only the negative sign from −2av³ gives 2av³, not 2av². Option 4 also has one power of v fewer, so reaching it needs a second error as well: stopping at dv/dx = −2av² without multiplying by v. As written the stated error does not produce the option the entry is attached to.
findings.fix: Stopping at dv/dx = −2av² and also dropping its negative sign, so that dv/dx is reported as the acceleration, giving 2av² instead of multiplying by v to get −2av³.

notes: Solved independently before reading the solution: dt/dx = 2ax + b, so v = 1/(2ax + b); dv/dx = −2a/(2ax + b)² = −2av²; acceleration = v dv/dx = −2av³, which is option 3. I checked this numerically with a = 0.3, b = 0.7 at x = 1.234 and the finite-difference values matched −2av² and −2av³ to seven figures. All four printed step equations are correct. common_mistakes[0] and [1] each name both of the changes needed to reach their option (a and b multiplied plus a lost power of v; b substituted for a plus a dropped sign), so only entry [2] is under-specified.
